The step that aligns the axis with ŷ divides by a zero axis norm or transverse axis length, although these maps admit a normal form and Forest's FPP handles them explicitly. For a synthetic map that rotates spin by 0.6 rad about ŷ, tilting the axis by 1e-9 rad returns the correct spin-tune magnitude 0.09549 but leaves a transverse quaternion component of 2.96e-10, because the alignment angle loses the tilt. The public `twiss(spin=true)` fails in checked planar rings and straight cells, including RF and coasting cases; the thick-bend quickstart ring escapes only through transverse round-off of order 1e-34.

title: Simultaneous magnetic-strength convention changes rescale the partner twice
summary: A magnetic strength can be set as a field (B) or normalized to rigidity (K), integrated or per unit length. Reassigning a nonzero strength its current value through a name that changes both choices at once rescales the unassigned normal or skew partner by an extra L or 1/L, where L is the element length; this self-assignment must preserve the field, as two successive single-change self-assignments do. For a proton dipole with L = 0.25 m, rigidity R = 7.3 T·m, `Bn0` = −0.21 T and `Bs0` = 0.13 T, assigning `Kn0L` its own value keeps the kick Δpx = 7.192×10⁻³ but reduces Δpy from 4.452×10⁻³, the uniform-field Lorentz-force value, to 1.113×10⁻³. A zero partner or L = 1 m hides the error.
